title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: Chapter 5: The Operator's Dashboard & the Ricks–Montarce Audit

epigraph.quote: We are in the early innings of a multi-decade transformation in how metabolic, neurodegenerative, and immune diseases are treated globally.
epigraph.author: David A. Ricks, Chair & CEO, Eli Lilly

web_blocks.html: Tracking Eli Lilly by lagging GAAP EPS alone misses the key drivers of long-term value. Lilly is scaling global plants, shifting U.S. payer access, and launching new drugs all at once. Investors should watch six leading operating KPIs every quarter.

web_blocks.takeaway: Five of six operational KPIs register a clear PASS, while realized net price (-15% YoY in Q3 2026) warrants active monitoring as commercial and government access widens.

web_blocks.html: Long-term room to grow remains huge even at a ~$91–$92 billion sales run-rate in late 2026. Over 800 million adults live with obesity and over 500 million live with diabetes worldwide. Yet branded incretin use stays in the low-to-mid single digits outside insured U.S. groups. Oral Foundayo's April 2026 approval removes cold storage and needle hurdles for primary-care doctors and emerging markets. Wider Medicare Part D obesity coverage and heart or sleep-apnea labels also open up older patient groups.
To test management's credibility, we audit CEO David A. Ricks (since January 2017) and CFO Lucas Montarce (since September 2024). We compare their 3-to-5-year public goals against audited results:

web_blocks.takeaway: Dave Ricks and Lucas Montarce have delivered on manufacturing, Foundayo approval, retatrutide, and guidance, but the $18.24B 9M 2026 BD/M&A surge places capital discipline on active WATCH.

web_blocks.html: Lilly's trial speed is another clear edge. From 2022 to 2026, it ran huge Phase 3 studies all at once: SURMOUNT (obesity), SURPASS (diabetes), ATTAIN/ACHIEVE (orforglipron), TRIUMPH (retatrutide), monarchE (breast cancer), and TRAILBLAZER-ALZ (Alzheimer's). It enrolled tens of thousands of patients with no major safety holds or FDA rejections on its core metabolic line. That steady pace cuts R&D timelines and stretches patent life.

On the risk side, payer-driven price drops remain the top watch item. Net prices dipped 5% YoY in Q4 2025, then fell 15% YoY in Q3 2026 as rebates, Medicare bridge deals, and overseas launches grew. Investors should watch if 2027 price drops settle in the high-single to low-double digits. If cuts deepen toward 20%+, Lilly will need >30% volume growth to keep profits rising.

Lilly's global staff grew to about 50,000 workers by late 2026 to run new plants, trials, and launches. Sales per worker topped $1.3 million in FY2025 and are tracking past $1.8 million in FY2026. Headcount growth has stayed tight next to top-line gains.

web_blocks.title: Q3 2026 Management Commentary (David A. Ricks, Chair & CEO)
paragraphs: "Lilly had another strong quarter, exceeding our prior expectations and allowing us to raise our full-year outlook," said David A. Ricks on October 29, 2026 [4]. "Revenue growth was driven by broad global consumer demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound, the global launches of Foundayo, expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care, and double-digit volume growth across our broader portfolio of medicines in oncology, immunology, and neuroscience." [4]

web_blocks.html: Lilly also paced its global rollout with care. Rather than flooding low-price markets early, it served U.S., European, and Japanese demand first. It then added KwikPens and oral Foundayo as new plants came online. That approach raised returns on tight supply and saved global upside for 2027–2030.

Governance and capital-allocation checks through November 2026 show a notable acceleration in external dealmaking alongside steady Endowment share reductions. Rather than remaining near ~$3 billion/year in IPR&D bolt-ons, Lilly deployed $18,240 million in 9M 2026 cash outflows for acquisitions ($10,692 million net cash for Centessa Pharmaceuticals at $5,958 million, Kelonia Therapeutics at $3,086 million, and Ventyx Biosciences at $1,058 million) and IPR&D ($7,548 million cash, including Q3 deals with AtaiBeckley and Curevo, plus post-quarter-end Merida Biosciences). Meanwhile, Schedule 13G/A (Amendment No. 47) shows Lilly Endowment Inc. reduced its stake from 92,190,516 shares (9.8% at Dec 31, 2025 per 2026 DEF 14A) to 90,066,978 shares (9.6% at Sept 30, 2026), while directors and executive officers as a group hold 1,362,076 shares (<1.0%).

book_paragraphs: Once you and I know how a business makes money and where its moat sits, the next job is building an operator's dashboard. In a hyper-growth pharmaceutical cycle, backward-looking earnings per share tell you what happened last year; leading operational KPIs tell you whether the engine is strengthening or quietly straining underneath.

At Eli Lilly, six operational indicators govern the next five years. First is global incretin volume growth—up 53% year-over-year in Q3 2026—which proves that underlying patient and physician demand is still expanding rapidly as supply opens up. Second, sitting right across the table from volume, is realized net price: down 15% year-over-year in Q3 2026. That price-versus-volume spread is the single most important operational ratio to watch.

As CEO David A. Ricks stated on October 29, 2026: 'Lilly had another strong quarter, exceeding our prior expectations and allowing us to raise our full-year outlook. Revenue growth was driven by broad global consumer demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound, the global launches of Foundayo, expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care, and double-digit volume growth across our broader portfolio.'

Our 2026 governance and capital-allocation audit flags two material updates. First, external business development accelerated sharply above the prior ~$3 billion annual pace: in 9M 2026, Lilly spent $10,692 million net cash on business combinations (Centessa, Kelonia, and Ventyx) plus $7,548 million on IPR&D asset deals (including AtaiBeckley and Curevo, followed by Merida Biosciences in Q4)—$18.24 billion combined. Second, Lilly Endowment Inc. trimmed its holdings by 2.12 million shares during 9M 2026, from 92.19 million shares (9.8%) to 90.07 million shares (9.6%), while executive officers and directors collectively hold under 1.0%.

book_subsections.title: Why Structural Penetration Is Still Early
paragraphs: It is easy to look at $91 billion to $92 billion in projected 2026 revenue and assume the market is saturated. In reality, global penetration of modern incretin therapies among clinically eligible obesity and Type 2 diabetes patients remains in the single digits. Hundreds of millions of patients worldwide cannot access refrigerated weekly pens due to cost, cold-chain infrastructure, or needle aversion.

That is why the April 2026 FDA approval of Foundayo (orforglipron) is a structural inflection, not just another product launch. A once-daily small-molecule pill that requires no refrigeration and no fasting window changes the unit economics of global primary care. Combined with expanding Medicare access for obesity with comorbidities like sleep apnea and cardiovascular disease, Lilly's volume runway remains unusually long—even as net prices per prescription step down.

book_subsections.title: The CEO & CFO Walk-the-Talk Audit
paragraphs: In institutional underwriting, we never take management's word on faith; we audit their past promises against audited results. When Dave Ricks took the helm in January 2017, he promised to focus Lilly's R&D on first-in-class or best-in-class science and avoid mega-mergers. Over the past five years, Ricks and CFO Lucas Montarce made four specific operational pledges: expand tirzepatide manufacturing capacity, bring oral orforglipron across the FDA finish line, advance triple-agonist retatrutide through Phase 3, and deploy capital via targeted bolt-on IPR&D rather than empire-building acquisitions.

Most of those operational pledges have been met or exceeded. Manufacturing capex scaled from $3.45 billion in 2023 to $7.84 billion in 2025, resolving FDA shortage designations. Orforglipron won FDA approval as Foundayo in April 2026, retatrutide cleared Phase 3 TRIUMPH trials ahead of a Q1 2027 filing, and FY2026 revenue guidance was raised three times—from $80–$83 billion in February to $91–$92 billion by October. The one yellow flag is external dealmaking: 9M 2026 BD and M&A cash outlays jumped to $18.24 billion versus the ~$3 billion annual baseline, putting capital discipline on active watch.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Discipline of Saying No to Mega-M&A
callouts.text: When pharmaceutical companies hit a cash windfall, boards often succumb to expensive external dealmaking. While Lilly avoided a single $50 billion mega-merger through 2025, its $18.24 billion nine-month 2026 surge in acquisitions and IPR&D warrants close scrutiny to ensure ROIC and free-cash-flow conversion stay intact.

book_subsections.title: What Could Break the Dashboard?
paragraphs: Every honest operator's dashboard needs a section on what breaks first if the thesis cracks. For Lilly, the first warning sign would not be a sudden collapse in prescriptions; it would be a narrowing of the price-volume scissors. Suppose commercial insurers tighten prior authorizations due to employer budget fatigue while Novo Nordisk and Amgen compete aggressively on rebates, pushing realized net price declines from -15% toward -22% just as volume growth slows from 53% toward 20%.

The second warning sign would be an unexpected safety signal in post-marketing surveillance for Foundayo or Phase 3 retatrutide—such as liver enzyme elevations, muscle-mass loss concerns, or severe gastrointestinal discontinuation rates—that slows primary-care adoption. Watching those two needles on the dashboard every quarter keeps you and I grounded in operational reality rather than market narrative.

book_subsections.title: The Next Wave of Clinical Catalysts (2027–2028)
paragraphs: Looking ahead from November 2026, management's next big test is the Q1 2027 regulatory filing for retatrutide and the global commercial scale-up of Foundayo outside the United States. If Lilly executes both while keeping Kisunla, Ebglyss, and Omvoh on double-digit sequential trajectories, its structural growth runway extends well into the 2030s.

book_subsections.title: Revenue per Employee and Organizational Scaling
paragraphs: One quiet metric on Lilly's operational scorecard is revenue per employee. With roughly 50,000 employees worldwide, Lilly generated about $1.3 million per employee in FY2025 and is tracking toward $1.8 million in FY2026. Most companies that triple revenue in four years suffer severe organizational bloat—layers of middle management, duplicated sales teams, and falling productivity. Lilly avoided that trap by scaling digital channels like LillyDirect and leaning on automated manufacturing lines rather than simply throwing headcount at growth.

Combine that operational discipline with Dave Ricks's and Lucas Montarce's spotless 2022–2026 execution record—resolving supply shortages, winning Foundayo approval in April 2026, advancing retatrutide toward a Q1 2027 filing, and raising 2026 revenue guidance three times—and you get a management team that has earned institutional trust.

book_subsections.title: Balancing Volume Velocity Against Net Price Realization
paragraphs: If you track only one operational ratio over the next eight quarters, track unit volume growth minus realized net price erosion. In Q3 2026, Lilly grew total volume by 53% while realized net prices declined 15%, producing 39% reported revenue growth. Because incremental manufacturing gross margins exceed 80%, volume expansion at three times the pace of price concessions drives massive operating leverage.

That spread is also our clearest early-warning sensor. If government Medicare negotiations, commercial PBM rebating, or rival launches from Novo Nordisk and Amgen compress realized net prices by more than 20% annually while volume growth slows toward 20%–25%, operating leverage would stall quickly. So far, CEO David A. Ricks and CFO Lucas Montarce have stayed ahead of guidance, raising FY2026 revenue to $91.0–$92.0 billion.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Watch the Price-Volume Ratio Every Quarter
book_callouts.text: Going forward, your checklist is simple: as long as incretin volume growth stays above 25%–30% while net price erosion stays contained in the single-to-mid-teens, and Foundayo plus Kisunla/Ebglyss/Omvoh scale smoothly, Lilly's operational thesis remains intact.
